content: Pullback strategy winner vs loser discriminators from quantitative research: (1) RSI level at entry — 2-day RSI < 20 generates highest Calmar ratio (0.63) for mean-reversion pullbacks; for trend-following pullbacks RSI 40-55 is optimal, extremes near 40 (oversold) or near 60 (still trending) correlate differently; (2) Volume contraction — low vol during pullback vs high vol during advance is primary quality signal; lower ratio = better winners; (3) Distance to support level — tighter proximity = better risk/reward = more winners; (4) Pullback depth — sweet spot around 8% from swing high; too shallow (momentum may not reset) or too deep (trend may be broken) both produce more losers; (5) ADX at entry — higher ADX (trend strength) = better pullback follow-through; (6) RS vs SPY — stocks with RS > 1.0 at entry have higher win rate; (7) Sector outperforming — acts as a tailwind. These are the seven metrics most worth bucketing in a winner vs loser analysis for pullback strategies.
